query: Starting from bulk HfNbTaTiZr, what single intervention could further reduce its lattice contribution to thermal conductivity relative to the unchanged material? Earlier studies examined heat transport in idealized fcc and bcc concentrated alloys using atomistic calculations, DFT coupled to analytical models, or Debye-based estimates. Most simulations treated perfect, defect-free bulk crystals, while experiments below 200 K inferred separate lattice and electronic contributions from thermal-conductivity and electrical-resistivity measurements. For HfNbTaTiZr, these contributions were estimated to have similar magnitudes from nearly 0 to 200 K; measurements from 300 to 1200 K instead concern a sample containing 1 wt.% oxygen, limiting direct comparison with the starting material. Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its physical mechanism, a quantitative or directional prediction relative to unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr, the temperature and material-state boundaries of the prediction, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that would falsify the hypothesis while separating lattice-mediated from electronic heat transport.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing lattice defects through ion irradiation can reduce the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity in bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
generation.mechanism: Introduction of lattice defects disrupts phonon transport, reducing lattice thermal conductivity
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 0-200 K, material state: single-phase solid solution
generation.uncertainty: Effect of ion irradiation on electronic thermal conductivity, potential for defect annealing at elevated temperatures

falsification_experiment.design: Measure thermal conductivity of ion-irradiated HfNbTaTiZr as a function of temperature and ion fluence
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If thermal conductivity increases with ion fluence or remains unchanged, the hypothesis is falsified

High thermal stability

The synthesized quinary W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEA shows high thermal stability in terms of grain coarsening. Even though there was an increase in the grain size during He implantation, the material preserved its nano-crystallinity and showed only approximately 10 nm change in grain size after ~8.45 at.% He implantation. The previously studied quaternary W-Ta-Cr-V RHEA demonstrated a similar thermal stability regarding grain morphology [22] . One of the properties that distinguishes this quinary W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf RHEA from the previously studied RHEAs is the grain refinement observed during dual-beam irradiation. Grain refinement was observed before in other materials [32] . Two main suggested mechanisms are discussed in the literature: (i) defect clusters produced during irradiation can migrate to sub-grain boundaries and form cell structures that lead to small grain formation [32] and (ii) cascades that are larger than the grain size can form stacking faults across the grain breaking it into two separate crystalline structures (observed in FCC material) [33] . High entropy alloys (HEAs) are a new class of metallic materials composed of multiple principle elements in equal or near-equal atomic proportions [1] , [2] . They have been receiving significant research interest owing to their exceptional mechanical and functional properties; see, e.g., refs [3] – [5] . Among various reported HEAs, the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi (Cantor alloy) [6] is a popular and important prototype of HEAs based on 3d transition metals. Within a wide range of temperature below its solidus, it usually forms a chemically disordered solid solution in face-centered cubic (fcc) structure at ambient pressure [6] – [9] . A unique mechanical characteristic of the Cantor alloy is an enhanced strength-ductility combination with decreasing temperature, while maintaining outstanding fracture toughness at cryogenic temperatures, which was demonstrated to be closely related to the formation of nano-twins and stacking faults in deformation [7] , [10] – [15] . Furthermore, due to the irreversible pressure-induced phase transition from the fcc to the hexagonal close-packed (hcp) lattice, the presence of the hcp structure was recently observed at ambient conditions [16] – [18] .
